name: Ish-bosheth
overview: Ish-bosheth was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin and is noted as a (illegitimate?) son of Saul. His identity is closely tied to his royal lineage, though specific details about his life beyond his parentage are sparse. He played a role in the early monarchy period of Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: Ish-bosheth means 'man of shame,' reflecting a name given without divine origin. He was also known by the name Eshbaal, meaning 'man of Baal,' and held the title 'King of Israel,' which denotes his brief reign over the nation. These names and titles highlight the complex cultural and religious context of his time.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Ish-bosheth as a son of Saul. He was ultimately killed by Baanah and Rimmon, indicating adversarial relationships that led to his death. No other family relationships are recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Ish-bosheth's significance lies in his role as a successor to Saul during a turbulent period in Israel's monarchy. His contested kingship and eventual assassination underscore the challenges of leadership and divine appointment in Israel's history. His story sets the stage for the rise of David as king, emphasizing God's providence in establishing His chosen ruler.
